doc: What the kernel prints for the host to read: `kith ls --json`, `kith project ls --json` (kernel/bin/kith-project) and `kith <agent> --launch-json` (kernel/bin/kith). Field names are the kernel's own snake_case. A model or effort is the harness's own word, which the host passes on as it came. Additive only: see serve/contract/README.md.

Harness.doc: The program an agent runs on: `harness:` in its agent.md (`claude-code` is printed as claude), or a backup entry's. The host starts claude, and codex for a backup entry. One this version doesn't know is its own state: the host doesn't start it.

PermissionMode.doc: The Claude Code permission mode a run starts in (kernel/lib/kith_settings.py CHOICES); a Codex run gets the host's translation. One this version doesn't know starts the run in default, which asks before every change.

Agent.doc: One agent in `kith ls --json`. `home` is its folder, where its bot works. A kernel from before `harness` was listed runs every agent on Claude.

Projects.doc: `kith project ls --json`: every registered project, sorted by id.

Project.doc: One registered project: its paths (absolute), its home folder when it has one, its git remotes, the project it sits in, its shared memory folder, and whether a folder of it is on this Mac.

Launch.doc: `kith <agent> --launch-json`: how to start the agent, for claude and codex. `settings` is Claude Code's settings (null for another harness), `mcp_servers` its servers in Claude's format, `claude_args` the arguments `kith <agent>` would give claude (null for another harness). `backup`, `provider` and `account` say which backup entry, harness and login answer the run; `account_id` is that login as a backup id (`claude`, `claude:work`, `codex`), the agent's main account or the `--backup` entry.

CostTag.doc: What the cost ledger files a run's usage under. `via` is where the run came from (terminal, serve, a channel).

launch.doc: How to start `agent` (run in the folder the run works in; `KITH_PERSON` makes it an invited person's run). `backup` launches a backup chain entry instead of the agent's own login; `project` loads that project's context.
